statement: WoodLog and Steel inherit ResourceBase.stackLimit=75; ComponentIndustrial explicitly overrides to 50.

ChunkGranite inherits stackLimit=1 and declares butcherProducts BlocksGranite=20; BlocksGranite inherits stackLimit=75. Project stone maps to abstract BlocksGranite material; mining directly yielding five is a project adaptation, not the original chunk process.
RawRice, RawPotatoes and RawCorn each inherit stackLimit=75; MealSimple and MealSurvivalPack inherit 10. These are distinct ThingDefs, not a shared raw-food stack identity.

Max hand carry count is min(stackLimit, RoundToInt(CarryingCapacity/VolumePerUnit)); VolumePerUnit defaults to 1 or 0.1 for smallVolume. The selected resource/food chains do not set smallVolume. This calculation does not divide by Mass.

CarryingCapacity has default base value 75 and minimum 1, with a BodySize stat part and Manipulation capacity factor weight 1. StatPart_BodySize multiplies by pawn body size; 75 is a baseline, not a universal pawn result.
CarryTracker uses a one-stack ThingOwner. Pickup is capped by job count, remaining hand stack space and source count; after a partial pickup, an unqueued source remainder reservation may be released.

Cell item capacity is edifice.MaxItemsInCell or 1 when no edifice exists; GetItemCount counts Item objects/stacks, not their units. Building reads maxItemsInCell and ShelfBase declares 3; this shelf value must not be applied to ordinary ground.

Normal storage accepts an existing compatible non-full stack even with no free stack slot; otherwise full item-slot count blocks placement. Base stacking requires non-destroyed Item, non-relic, same Def and Stuff, with ThingComp checks able to reject it.
GetItemStackSpaceLeftFor sums same-Def stack deficits plus max(cell capacity minus Item count,0)*def.stackLimit. It is a count estimate, not a substitute for complete CanStackWith compatibility.

Standard HaulToCell pre-reserves destination cell then source with maxPawns=1 and stackCount=-1. ReservationManager resolves a cell to quantity1 and -1 to full available target quantity; IsGoodStoreCell rejects another respected reservation, static fire, blockers and unreachable destination. This is not a future-storage quantity ledger.
HaulToCellStorageJob counts available capacity across its slot/storage group; fitInStoreCell=false can gather enough for multiple destination cells. Pickup still clamps to hand and source limits.

GenPlace Direct first merges into compatible stacks (largest stacks first), then splits at stackLimit into available slots. False may mean a partial transfer, with a remainder still unplaced. Direct has a special extra-slot fallback for stackLimit<=1, so ordinary storage validation and raw placement are different contracts.

GenPlace Near selects locations through initial9 cells, radius3 and radius12.9 bands, checking spawn suitability, validator, storage acceptance, item slots and stackability. It loops after a partial transfer while stack count changes; this is not an unbounded map search.

ThingOwner TryDrop removes its contained thing only after GenDrop reports success; GenDrop delegates to GenPlace. A Direct partial failure keeps the remainder in the owner while already placed portions remain placed.

Haul drop failure/partial completion can seek another store cell and continue with the remainder; if none, it tries HaulAside. The extreme final branch logs a warning and destroys the carried item. Preserving blocked cargo instead is an explicit safer project adaptation.

Automatic better-storage selection uses a strictly higher priority than current and then approximate distance search within eligible groups. Original priorities are Unstored0,Low1,Normal2,Preferred3,Important4,Critical5; temperature is not part of this selection.

Priority setter resorts destinations and recalculates haulables. An already active HaulToCell checks IsValidStorageFor while going to source/carrying: presence, filter and blockers, not whether another priority became preferable. Priority-only changes do not by these checks alone force immediate reroute.

Raw GenSpawn is not a transactional stockpile-capacity API: when spawning an Item into a full playing-map cell it may despawn one existing Item and try to move it Near, destroying it if that fails. ThingGrid is a list registry, not the storage-capacity enforcement layer.
